text:
maria: Hi team — customer hitting a 413 from our /v1/rerank endpoint. Payload ~1.2MB, but weirdly some candidates are coming back with 0.0 scores while others score normally. Any quick ideas? :thinking:

devon: which field contains the query? can you paste a minimal repro? 413 means request too large, but the scoring oddness is separate.

maria: minimal snippet below — note we accidentally shoved the `query` inside each doc under `meta.query`, not at the top-level. curl + response: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"collection":"kb","candidates":[{"id":"1","text":"...","meta":{"query":{"q":"how to reset"}}},{"id":"2","text":"..."}],"limit":100}'
```

HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large
content-type: application/json
{ "error": "request entity too large" }
```

maria: also server logs show these lines when the 0.0 scores happen: `Missing query context for candidate id=1, defaulting to 0.0`

sam: that log is helpful — rerank expects a single `query` string at the request root or `query` key in the top-level `items` object. If you bury it under `meta` inside each candidate we treat that as metadata, not the search query. That explains the 0.0.

luis: FWIW we do have a hard request body limit at the edge (1MB) that returns 413. For large candidate sets use: 1) batch requests, 2) pass only candidate ids and call our `candidate-batch` service, or 3) compress the payload with gzip at the client and set `Content-Encoding: gzip` (we accept it).

devon: @maria can you try moving query to root like this? 

```json
{
  "collection":"kb",
  "query":"how to reset",
  "candidates":[{"id":"1","text":"..."},{"id":"2","text":"..."}],
  "limit":100
}
```

maria: testing that now... trying smaller batches first to avoid 413. will update. :running:

maria: OK moved query out, rerun succeeded for batch size 100, scores look sensible now. no 0.0s.

luis: great — follow-up notes: we should improve error message when query is missing (instead of silently scoring 0.0). I filed a tiny issue: RERANK-3189 to surface `missing_query` in response with guidance.

ops-bot: Incident ping — RERANK-3189 created by luis. Priority: P3. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RERANK-3189

devon: Thanks — marking this resolved for the customer. Suggested customer reply: "We found the issue — the `query` field must be at the request root. We recommend batching or gzipping large candidate lists to avoid 413." :thumbsup:
